body:
> Observed 2026-08-28 on #134: blocked from the operator's shell one minute after claim; its agent
> kept working for ten more minutes and would have run to `--max-turns`/`--max-budget-usd`.

## Why

`reapDecision` (`src/dispatch.js:305`) stops an agent whose task is finished, leaves a *running*
task's agent to the reclaim step, and on any other live status spares the agent **while it is
genuinely working**. The comment says why: a worker that has just filed its terminal verb is still
writing its last turn and must not be cut off mid-push.

That rule assumes the attempt ended from *inside* the session. When a terminal verb is run from
outside — `hkb block <n>` by an operator, `hkb adopt --status`, a reconcile that moved the card —
the attempt row is closed, the lock is gone, and the agent has no lease. `jobWorking(job)` is still
true, so the reaper spares it indefinitely. The agent finishes its work, runs a verb that has no open
attempt to land on, and every token in between was spent on a task the board had already taken away.

## What

Bound the grace, and make it about the attempt, not the process state.

- The reaper sees the run record (the caller already loads it). When the task's latest attempt is
  **ended** and the agent is still working, spare it for a short grace window — enough to finish a
  push, say 2–3 minutes after `ended_at` — then stop it with a reason that says so:
  `its attempt ended at <t> (<outcome>) and the agent is still working — stopping after grace`.
- A worker that just filed its own verb is covered by the same window; nothing else changes for it.
- `hkb block`/`unblock`/`adopt` run from outside a worker session could say, in their one-liner, that
  a live agent will be stopped on the next tick — so the operator is not surprised either way.

## Done when

- A task blocked from outside while its agent works: the agent is stopped within one tick after the
  grace window, and the dispatch log names the reason.
- A worker that files its own verb and keeps writing for a minute is not cut off.
- `node --test test/reap.test.js` covers both, with a deterministic clock.
goal: an agent whose attempt was ended by an operator verb is stopped after a short grace window
title: An attempt ended from outside the session leaves its agent working with no lease
